userEnteredValue.stringValue: The NCCER/Build Your Future contribution funds the same AGC Workforce Development scholarship represented at Master row 144. Awards are up to $1,000 per year and renewable for up to two years, subject to continuing enrollment and good standing (2.5 GPA or equivalent). Students including high school seniors may pursue approved accredited construction degrees, certificates, craft training or registered apprenticeships full- or part-time; U.S. citizenship or permanent residency is required. userEnteredValue.stringValue: National Aviation Explorer Scholarship2026 requires active registered Aviation Explorer post membership. Submit all materials together by email using the official PDF, at least three non-family recommendations and educational/career essay; under18 applicants need a parent/guardian signature. Leadership, aviation accomplishments and achievement are selection factors. Five categories cover aviation degree, avionics, pilot certification, maintenance and management. Applicants may request multiple categories but receive only one scholarship per academic year. The introduction says two2500scholarships while five types each describe2500; this does not guarantee five awards. Degree applicants must be accepted/attending accredited aviation college/university and redeem within four years. Avionics/maintenance permit HSseniors entering relevant accredited programs; management requires an accredited aviation-management program. These three redeem within two years. Sport/private pilot training need not be career-oriented; finish training within one year and redeem within two. DeadlineApril30,2026; future cycle, numericGPA, generalage/citizenship and fee conditions are unverified.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: DEWALT Trades Scholarship, administered with SKILLED Nation, supports students enrolled in or accepted to a postsecondary school or training program in a high-demand skilled trade in the United States or Canada. Listed fields span construction, industrial maintenance/manufacturing, motor/power, mechanics including aviation mechanics/avionics, and technology including electrical engineering, CAD, fire science and mechatronics. Employees of Stanley Black & Decker or DEWALT and their spouses/dependents are excluded. Awards are paid to the school or training center. The 2026 application opened November 4, 2025 and closed February 28, 2026; late applications are ineligible. This is the US application route; Canada has a separate linked route. No next-cycle date, GPA threshold or renewal guarantee is established.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: The Pell Promise for Montana Students is a financial aid initiative by Carroll College for Montana residents who are Federal Pell Grant recipients. It provides significant financial assistance, covering tuition, to eligible students who maintain a 3.0 GPA, reside on-campus, and accept a federal Stafford loan. It aims to enhance accessibility and affordability for under-served Montanans pursuing a Catholic, liberal arts education.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: The current Carroll Pell Promise page describes fall 2027 first-time freshmen and transfer students residing in the U.S., living on campus, qualifying for Pell through FAFSA, maintaining a 3.0 GPA and completing at least 12 credits per semester, for up to eight semesters. Tuition support combines federal aid, Carroll merit/need gift aid and subsidized Stafford borrowing; it is not all grant funding or a guarantee of full tuition. The introductory steps say to agree to borrow $3,500, while detailed criteria assume maximum subsidized loans of $3,500/$4,500/$5,500 by year; this wording difference remains unresolved. Summer/winter tuition, study abroad and fees are excluded; additional criteria and athletic-aid exceptions may apply. These current 2027 terms differ from the unavailable historical Montana-only 2026 page.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: STEAM Generator Scholarship supports students pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in a STEAM field. Its eligibility paragraph allows first- or second-generation immigrants, or otherwise underrepresented minorities in higher education whose parents and grandparents have not attained the level being pursued. The placement of the family-degree condition does not clearly establish whether it also applies to the immigrant branch. The essay specifically asks about first- or second-generation immigrant experience, although the eligibility paragraph includes another minority pathway; instructions for that pathway remain unclear. Applicants submit400–600words about entering higher education and their background. The public Apply Now control links to Bold.org signup. The deadline is November30,2026; three awards are1055dollars each. This is a conditional degree-program opportunity, not confirmed for a high-school-only applicant before undergraduate study. No GPA, income threshold or renewal guarantee is established.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: Montana STEM/Healthcare Scholarship Program is for Montana residents applying in the year they graduate from a high school accredited by the Montana Board of Public Education. It requires at least a 3.25 cumulative high-school GPA, four years of college-prep math and three years of college-prep science. Students must be accepted at an eligible campus, declare a qualifying STEM or healthcare major, seek their first certificate, two-year or four-year degree, enroll in at least 12 credits each semester and begin in the fall immediately after graduation. Apply through AwardMontana by March 15 (cycle year not stated), with the seventh-semester transcript, acceptance proof and counselor-signed math/science certification. Awards are $1,000 in year one, $1,500 in years two and three and $2,000 in year four if continuing requirements are met; not every program necessarily lasts four years.

The program seeks advocacy and leadership, engagement in mental-health or disability rights, inclusivity, creativity and a strong academic record. It also calls for personal experience with mental health or disability through oneself, family or community; a diagnosis or the applicant's own condition is not stated as mandatory. Applicants submit400–600words about advocacy in the Asian American community and their goals, and upload an image of themselves helping or a school portrait. The exact page displays Apply Now to Bold.org signup. Two500-dollar awards have a December7,2026 deadline. Numeric GPA, service-hours and income thresholds and renewal conditions are not stated. High-school-only eligibility is not confirmed; this is a conditional undergraduate opportunity.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: Donald E. Pizzini Memorial Nurse Scholarships provide up to $2,500 for full-time or part-time accredited nursing degree or certificate study relevant to long-term care. Applicants must be US citizens or permanent residents, reside in Montana, plan to work or remain working in Montana long-term-care nursing, and be available for a qualifying interview. A 3.0 prior GPA is required, using high-school GPA for first-year students; the committee may waive it for current long-term-care professionals based on work performance and experience. Acceptance or enrollment proof, official transcripts and two non-family recommendations are required. Preference goes to current long-term-care workers or those interested in that career, and people with current or past MHCA-member-facility employment. Use the official Initial Scholarship Application PDF for applicants who have not previously received this award. Applications are due the last day of February, with awards in April for the coming academic year; the year is unstated. Enrollment and continued participation must be proved for payments; the committee may withhold/cancel funds below3.0. Recipients may reapply after their award expires; renewal is not guaranteed.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: The Dennis & Phyllis Washington Foundation's Horatio Alger Montana Undergraduate Scholarship provides up to $15,000 over four years for students who have overcome adversity. Its detailed eligibility still specifies full-time Montana high-school seniors graduating in spring/summer 2026, entering the Montana University System no later than the following fall, US citizenship, critical financial need, integrity/perseverance and co-curricular, after-school or community activity involvement. Pell-eligible families are encouraged; Pell eligibility is not stated as mandatory. Recipients must pursue and complete a bachelor's degree but may start at a two-year institution and transfer. Eligible institutions include UM, MSU and the named Montana affiliates. The page gives December 1–February 15 for seniors and December 1–March 1 for juniors; junior eligibility details and the next cycle year are not fully stated. Apply through Horatio Alger; an existing National Scholarship application is automatically considered. Recipients maintain a 2.0 GPA to keep the award; this is a renewal condition, not a verified entrance minimum. The current page does not substantiate the older $10,000 plus $5,000 split.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: Beginning in 2026, the former Joseph James Morelli Legacy Foundation scholarship is available only to students attending Montana State University. The foundation states that it is dissolving and transferring to MSU, which will award the four-year Hilleman/Morelli Scholarship to STEM students demonstrating learning differences, selected for academic, leadership and career potential. It combines financial, academic, leadership and mentoring support. The foundation directs applicants to the Hilleman Scholars application page, whose public instructions reference students starting MSU in Fall 2026. The application extraction did not expose Morelli-specific instructions. A Morelli-specific award amount, deadline, GPA minimum, learning-difference documentation standard, Montana residency requirement, renewal conditions and next-cycle availability are not verified. The foundation historically served students with dyslexia, but the new award uses broader learning-differences wording. This is a distinct named program from the general Hilleman scholarship; its conditions and amount must not be assumed identical.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: The MUS Honor Scholarship waives tuition, excluding fees, at an eligible Montana campus for up to eight semesters, subject to continuing requirements. The 2027 application opens December 1, 2026 and is due March 15, 2027. Applicants must be Montana residents graduating that year, have attended an accredited Montana high school for at least three years including senior year, have at least 3.4 GPA after seven semesters, complete the Rigorous Core or IB diploma and be accepted by an eligible campus. ACT or SAT testing is required: the current application step says February 2027, but one proof checklist still says February 2026, so the test-year detail remains unresolved. Apply through Award Montana and complete the listed supporting-document steps. Selection is competitive and funding is not guaranteed.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: KPMG Future Leaders2025 supported female high-school seniors, including homeschooled students, graduating2024–25 and entering a four-year undergraduate program by fall2025. Business or STEM study,3.5GPA and a financial-need essay with household income no more than75000 were required. userEnteredValue.stringValue: This scholarship is open for students pursuing associate degrees, technical training, or certificates to enter the construction industry.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: The AGC/NCCER Workforce Development scholarship supports full- or part-time students, including high school seniors, who intend a construction career and enroll or intend to enroll in an approved accredited construction degree, certificate, craft training or registered apprenticeship program. U.S. citizenship or permanent residency is required. Awards are up to $1,000 per year, renewable for up to two years subject to continuing enrollment and good standing (2.5 GPA or equivalent for renewal). The 2026–27 form requires a fall 2026 class and is closed; its June 1 deadline time conflicts between the header and body. Master row 146 represents the same program; consolidation remains a separate unapplied recommendation. Students pursuing a four-year bachelor's degree must use the separate AGC Undergraduate Scholarship application rather than this Workforce Development program.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: MSU Hilleman Scholars is a program for Montana residents who are recent Montana high-school graduates with academic, leadership and career potential. The official application is labeled Fall 2026 without an exact deadline; the details page describes selection by invitation and still contains a 2025 orientation date. The program offers $4,000 per year for four years, conditional on academic progress and 10–15 hours each week of mentoring, learning, internship and community development activities. Completion of the Summer Success Academy is required to retain the offer, with a separate $2,000 academy stipend. The stated group study-abroad support is conditional. Hilleman cannot be stacked with Horatio Alger funding. Neither Pell eligibility nor first-generation status is established as a mandatory requirement by the checked public rules.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: Graduating high school senior, Completed FVCC college application. To be eligible to apply for the FVCC Eagle Scholarship, students must have applied as a new incoming, degree-seeking student for the upcoming fall semester. Students will be awarded based on their most recent cumulative GPA (either high school or college for transfer students), HiSET or GED Scores.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: Soroptimist Live Your Dream Awards are for women who provide primary financial support for themselves and their dependents and have financial need. Applicants must be enrolled in or accepted to a vocational/skills training or undergraduate degree program and be motivated to achieve their education and career goals. High-school-equivalency study alone is not listed as an eligible program. Dependents may include children, spouse, partner, siblings or parents. Applicants must reside in a Soroptimist International of the Americas member country or territory, including the United States; previous Women's Opportunity or Live Your Dream recipients, people with or pursuing a graduate degree, Soroptimist members, employees and their immediate family are ineligible. Applications run August 1–November 15 (cycle year not stated). Club awards vary; selected recipients may progress to regional and international levels, for a potential total of $1,000–$16,000. Written sections must reflect the applicant's own experiences and goals; AI may help grammar or organization. Apply through the official Soroptimist application portal.

Applicants need financial support and must have applied to or be enrolled in a postsecondary degree/certificate, including trade or technical study. Priority goes to those with limited access to family wealth. This requires specific movement-organizing work, beyond general volunteering or interest. Recipients must reapply each year. No political affiliation response is collected or inferred by this system.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: HPFY Beyond Disability Scholarship supports high-school seniors and current college students living with a documented disability. Seniors must plan undergraduate study in a US two-year, four-year or technical college in the fall following graduation; full-time and part-time enrollment are allowed. GPA does not affect selection. The official FAQ directs an email application by August 15 without a cycle year, with proof of enrollment, disability documentation, an essay of at least 500 words about disability-related experiences and optional supporting recommendations. Selection is based on the essay and documentation. The provider publishes the selected recipient on its website. Current-cycle availability and renewal terms are not established. This is distinct from HPFY Make a Difference, which is already in Master.

userEnteredValue.stringValue: Eligible students: Senior girls in Flathead County Public High Schools in 2025 who are planning to attend college or university. Criteria: financial need, academic ability, and those seeking a career that aligns with the mission of Soroptimist International. Our mission statement is "A global volunteer organization that provides women and girls with access to the education and training they need to achieve economic empowerment." Priority given to girls planning to attend in-state programs (but it is NOT a requirement!).

Priority is given to financial need and academic success; Montana colleges and universities are preferred, not required. Awards range from $1,000 to $3,000. The deadline was April 17, 2026; the linked form is closed and says it will accept applications in spring 2027, without a published 2027 deadline. An older 2024 application excluded children of club members; the full 2026 family restriction is unavailable in the closed form and remains unconfirmed.

tagStorage: Reviewed local ledger metadata keyed by stable entity ID only; no tag cells, extra columns, runtime questions, matching rules or publication changes.

inversePlan.perOperation: Restore full native preimages from the future verified affected-cell backup only when each current affected cell still matches the exact reviewed post-write fingerprint. Clear appended selected values/runs back to their empty preimage; do not delete rows. Preserve unrelated later edits.
inversePlan.selectedPreimages: Each operation includes the original selected native value/formula/rich-link projection for comparison; complete format/validation/protection preimages remain a mandatory future private backup gate.
inversePlan.wholeWorkbook: Emergency recovery source only; no automatic replacement/deletion/rename/repoint. Exact restore authority, snapshot of current state and reconciliation of intervening edits required.

reconciliation.required: Read every targeted native cell and row identity plus bounded unaffected ranges; compare values, formulas/rich-links, operation IDs, append placement and duplicate counts. API success alone is not reconciliation.
reconciliation.onUncertain: Stop; read only to distinguish not applied, fully applied, partial or conflicting. Never blindly retry or automatically roll back.
reconciliation.publication: Workbook changes do not update the immutable website publication; a future separately selected mapping/release is required.
